key_insight: Reliable a posteriori error estimators quantify finite element errors in evolution equations with memory without exponentially growing time factors.
engineering_relevance: These estimators can guide adaptive simulations of history-dependent diffusion and wave-like dynamics while controlling spatial and temporal discretization errors.
method: Time-dependent finite element spaces with backward Euler integration and memory quadrature.
Elliptic reconstruction for optimal spatial error estimates.
Cancellation-preserving memory-lag analysis for first-order temporal estimation.
evidence_signal: Numerical experiments on a convex domain validate the theory, and space-time adaptivity is demonstrated on an L-shaped domain with a corner singularity and two temporal layers.
watch_item: The theory assumes bounded convex polygonal or polyhedral domains; the nonconvex L-shaped example demonstrates adaptivity beyond that stated setting.
paper_title: A Posteriori Error Analysis of Finite Element Approximation to an Evolution Equation with a Positive-Type Memory Term
